findings.title: KeyError crash when an existing Integration has no "sender" in metadata
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when an Integration row exists for the installation_id but has no OrganizationIntegration, the new verification does `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`. The "sender" key is only written into metadata by the installation webhook; `build_integration` adds it only when the pipeline state contains "sender", and nothing in the pipeline ever binds that key, so every integration created through the pipeline path (e.g. when the webhook was delayed or lost) lacks it, as do older rows created before the webhook recorded the sender. If such an integration later loses its OrganizationIntegration (e.g. the region-side org integration is deleted while the control-side Integration row is still ACTIVE during deletion propagation) and a user tries to install again, this line raises KeyError and returns a 500 instead of the intended failure page, blocking legitimate reinstalls. Use a guarded lookup such as `integration.metadata.get("sender", {}).get("login")` and explicitly fail closed with the error page when the sender is unknown.

findings.title: Unguarded GitHub API calls in OAuthLoginView can 500 the install pipeline
findings.body: The code exchange (`safe_urlopen(url=ghip.get_oauth_access_token_url(), data=data)`) and the profile fetch (`get_user_info(payload["access_token"])`) are not wrapped in any exception handling. safe_urlopen raises requests exceptions on connection errors/timeouts, and get_user_info can raise if GitHub returns a non-JSON error response. Any of these transient failures propagate as unhandled exceptions and the user gets a 500, which is inconsistent with the goal of this PR to show the "Invalid installation request" page whenever GitHub verification cannot be completed. Wrap both calls and render `error(request, self.active_organization)` on failure.

findings.title: No test covers the sender-match success path of the new verification
findings.body: test_github_user_mismatch only exercises the failure branch of the new check (authenticated GitHub user differs from the recorded installation sender). No test covers the complementary case where the Integration exists without an OrganizationIntegration and the authenticated user matches `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]`, verifying that installation then proceeds. In all success-path tests the Integration row is absent at check time, so the verification code is never exercised positively. Given that this check reads nested metadata that may be missing on some rows, a success-path test with an existing sender-recorded integration would catch regressions in both directions.
